newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast Lt. crudes up after ANS cargo sells.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast Lt. crudes up after ANS cargo sells.

text.p: U.S. West Coast Alaskan crude prices rose Wednesday after BP America sold a full cargo to a Pacific Northwest refiner, traders said.

The cargo, weighing 300,000 barrels, cost $1.18 under benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI). The deal, confirmed by both parties, posted a 12 cent-increase over the last cargo, which sold Tuesday at a discount of $1.30.
After falling early with WTI, spot trade for ANS ended the day $22.62/22.82 a barrel, as the narrowing discount offset a 10-cent drop in March WTI, the basis for Alaskan crudes.
BP indicated its next cargo at $1.10 under WTI.
